Subject: Interested in a short demo — CartFlow checkout use case

Hi Priyom,

I signed up through the self-serve flow this morning and wanted to follow up to schedule a short demo. We're evaluating inference providers for an in-checkout personalization and fraud-scoring flow (server-side). High-level: ~6m monthly checkout events, expected peak concurrency around 30 qps during promos, typical model response ~350 tokens. Goal is to reduce latency under 120ms p95 and get clear cost estimates for steady-state vs peak.

Timeline: aiming to start an evaluation in November and a pilot in December if things look good.

Available this week afternoons ET. Can you share a 30-min slot? Also fine to answer a few quick fit questions up-front.

Thanks,
Alex Jenkins
Head of Platform
CartFlow

+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cartflow.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-06T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Interested in a short demo — CartFlow checkout use case

Alex — thanks for signing up and the context. Quick note from my side before we lock a time: I usually ask a few targeted questions so the demo is focused and we can bring the right engineer if needed. Short answers are totally fine.

1) Is the model inference call synchronous within the checkout path (blocking checkout) or async (precompute/ranking)?
2) Average tokens per request and tokens of context (prompt + history)? You mentioned ~350 for response — what's the typical prompt size?
3) Expected p95 latency target (you said 120ms; is that strict for peak as well?)
4) Any data sensitivity (PII / payment data) or enterprise controls required (VPC, audit logs, SOC-2 evidence)?
5) Stakeholders who need to attend the demo (engineering, security, product)?
6) Preferred demo length: 30 or 45 minutes?

If you can drop a quick CSV with hourly/weekday traffic for a typical week (sample header idea attached below) that helps us pick the right runtime and slot. I attached a one-row CSV template you can fill and reply.

Slot buckets I can offer this week (all ET):
- Tue 10/6: 2:00–2:30pm or 4:00–4:30pm
- Wed 10/7: 11:00–11:30am or 3:30–4:00pm
- Thu 10/8: 10:00–10:30am (preferred for engineering presence)

If none work, share two times that work and I'll try to match. Also happy to send a calendar link if you want to pick.

Attachment: traffic_sample_template.csv (1-line sample) — please fill and reply.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
SDR, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
[attachment: traffic_sample_template.csv (text/csv)]

From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cartflow.com>

Subject: Re: Interested in a short demo — CartFlow checkout use case

On Tue, Oct 6, 2026 at 11:05 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for signing up and the context. Quick note from my side before we lock a time: I usually ask a few targeted questions so the demo is focused and we can bring the right engineer if needed. Short answers are totally fine.

Hi Priyom — thanks for the thorough list. Answers inline below.

1) Synchronous (blocking) — we call the model in the critical path; any extra latency directly impacts conversion.
2) Prompt + context ~450 tokens (we include last 3 interactions), response ~300–400 tokens depending on personalization depth.
3) 120ms p95 is our ideal target; for promos we can tolerate up to 200ms p95 but would expect graceful degradation (fallback) beyond that.
4) Contains PII (email hash, order id) but not raw card data; SOC-2 & audit logs are required for any pilot. VPC + KMS would be preferred.
5) Stakeholders: me (platform), 1x infra eng (Lina Ortega), and 1x product manager (Samir Patel). Lina and Samir are flexible on time.
6) 30 minutes should be fine.

Attached sample traffic file (hourly averages for the last week) — filename: cartflow_traffic_sample.csv. Peak spikes show weekends and promotional days.

Proposed times (ET):
- Thu 10/8 10:00–10:30am
- Fri 10/9 11:00–11:30am

If Thu 10/8 10:00 works, let's take that one.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Jenkins
Head of Platform, CartFlow
